meta.title: Formatting needs to leave space between consecutive less-than tokens <
meta.fix_ref: microsoft/TypeScript#32088 (Merge pull request #32088 from orta/fix-32068), a50a5d309c, 2019-06-26; git tag --contains: first in v3.6-beta / v3.6.2
meta.build_notes: npm typescript@3.5.3 (2019-07-08) and typescript@3.6.2 (2019-08-28), both behind typescript-language-server@0.4.0 (the latest wrapper release before 3.6.2), started with the pinned tsserver.js; the reported TypeScript version is checked on every session. Wrapper 0.4.0 is installed with the dependencies of its release date (install_builds.wrapper_before). The wrapper logs no TypeScript version; the build check verifies that its tsserver child runs the pinned tsserver.js.
meta.notes: '<number>foo <<number>bar' still parses (a shift followed by a comparison), so the damage shows as new type errors ('number' only refers to a type), hence edit_leaves_diagnostic with that message as the target; foo and bar are undeclared in the issue's snippet, which gives the same errors before and after.

settings_note: The issue names no settings; FormattingOptions are the probe defaults (4 spaces); no tsconfig.json.

files.source: issue body, first typescript code block
files.note: the file name is not given in the issue

repro.steps: Open index.ts and format the document (Alt+Shift+F). Reported: 'if (<number>foo < <number>bar)' becomes 'if (<number>foo <<number>bar)', which no longer compiles (a second format gives '<< number > bar'). Probe: after the whole-document format, a fresh session on the edited file must not report an error the case session did not report before; the target is the resulting "'number' only refers to a type" error.
